# Measured combinations

Which component works under which method, **measured**: every cell of this page is a
recorded run of [`grasppanda compose` and `grasppanda probe`](../user_guides/combinations.md),
and nothing is inferred from a contract or from another cell. The contract tables of
[Swapping components](swapping.md) say what the config check accepts; this page says
what happened when the accepted combinations were built, trained and asked to predict.

**No AP appears on this page, and none follows from it.** A probe trains 20 iterations
on 8 frames. It shows whether a combination *works*: it builds, its losses are finite,
seeds reach its head, it predicts. It says nothing about how good the combination is;
that takes a full training run and an evaluation on a benchmark split.

## What was run

- **Grid**: 915 cells (706 `runs`, 11 `runs-unstable`, 192 `refused`, 6 `fails`): every shipped method config as it is, every registered scene encoder under every seed-based method, every variant of every other stage with one stage replaced at a time, the legal sets of stage variants, HGGD as it is, and every image-encoder preset under HGGD. The variants of a stage are its presets plus every component whose constructor defaults no preset states.
- **A cell**: `grasppanda compose <method config> --set <slot>=<choice>`, so that an encoder is fitted and adapters are inserted exactly as a user gets them, then `grasppanda probe <composed config> --iters 20 --frames 8`: the real trainer with the method's own recipe on the split `sample` of GraspNet-1Billion (RealSense; scene 0, frames 0, 32, …, 224), then prediction on two of those frames. Both commands of every cell are in the [measured file](measured_combinations.json).
- **One exception to "as a user gets them"**: configs that read the width histogram of Scale-Balanced-Grasp were probed with the reference's own file (`scale_statistic.source: legacy_import`), because the native histogram is a statistic of the whole training split and a probe reads eight frames. The override is part of the recorded command.
- **When and where**: 167 cells on 2026-10-13 with GraspPanda at commit `e849e98`, PyTorch 2.7.1+cu118, Python 3.12.7, on one NVIDIA RTX A6000 shared with other jobs, 2 probes at a time. 16 cells on ## Verdicts

| Verdict | In a table | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `runs` | ✓ · ✓ own · ✓ in `Adapter` | On real frames: the detector was built, every requested training iteration ran with finite losses and at least one real seed, the weights stayed finite, and prediction returned valid grasp groups for every probed frame. |
| `runs-unstable` | ≈ (n) | On real frames: training and prediction ran to the end, but a loss or a weight became non-finite, or an iteration had no real seed (no scene point passed the proposal, so only the proposal was trained), or no iteration supervised a seed. |
| `refused` | ✗ (n) | The config check refused the config (the same check as `grasppanda print-config --check --for train`). Nothing was built; the report carries the messages. On this page all 192 refusals come from `grasppanda compose`, which runs that check on the composed config and writes nothing when it fails. |
| `fails` | **fails** (n) | An exception was raised after the config check had passed. The report names the phase (build, data, optimizer, loss, backward, step, hook, predict), the component it came from and the message. |
| `wired` | — | No real frame was read. On a synthetic table-top scene with random labels the detector was built, back-propagated a loss through every stage and predicted. This shows that the stages connect; it says nothing about real data. Not used on this page. |

*✓ in `Adapter`*: the bare swap is refused by the contract between encoder and proposal; compose wrapped the encoder in the one adapter that bridges it, said so, and the adapted config ran. *†*: compose also fitted the encoder to the method, setting `out_channels` to the width of the encoder it replaces or `in_channels` to the point features the method feeds. *(n)* points to the reason below the table: for a refusal the first sentence of each message of the config check (the whole messages, with the fix they propose, are in the measured file), for a failure the phase, the component and the exception, for an unstable run what was unstable. *‡* marks numbers that depend on the load of a shared machine.

## Measured classes

A component **works** under a method when its cell is `runs` or `runs-unstable`: the combination was built, trained for the probe's iterations and predicted, directly or in the adapter compose inserted. The class of a component counts the seed-based methods (GSNet, EconomicGrasp, FineGrasp, GraspNet-baseline, Scale-Balanced-Grasp) it works under:

- **universal**: it works under all five seed-based methods.
- **most**: it works under three or four of them.
- **some**: it works under two.
- **specific**: it works under exactly one.
- **none**: it works under none of them as it was probed.

*≈n* after a class: under n of those methods the run was `runs-unstable`; the note under the table says what was unstable. A class is a statement about this grid: these presets, the methods' own recipes, this dataset, one stage replaced at a time. A stage that is refused alone may work together with the stage it depends on (a head bundle with its assigner and its labels); those are the [sets of stages](#sets-of-stages).

### Encoder adapters

An adapter wraps an encoder and is not one itself, so it has no row above: compose inserts it where the contract between encoder and proposal asks for it (`✓ in Adapter`). What was measured with each, over all groups of the grid:

| Adapter | Cells it was inserted in | `runs` | `runs-unstable` | `refused` | `fails` | Under |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `FeaturePropagation`<br>preset `feature-propagation` | 64 | 32 | — | 32 | — | GSNet, EconomicGrasp, FineGrasp, GraspNet-baseline, Scale-Balanced-Grasp |
| `FurthestPointSubsample`<br>preset `furthest-point-subsample` | 85 | 85 | — | — | — | GSNet, EconomicGrasp, FineGrasp, GraspNet-baseline, Scale-Balanced-Grasp |

1. OperationHead as configured reads the seed score 'objectness' when it decodes, but neither SubsampledSeeds nor DirectionViewStage predicts it.
2. OperationHead as configured reads the seed score 'objectness' when it decodes, but neither SubsampledSeeds nor HealpixViewStage predicts it.
3. OperationHead as configured reads the seed score 'objectness' when it decodes, but neither SubsampledSeeds nor IcosphereViewStage predicts it.
4. OperationHead as configured reads the seed score 'objectness' when it decodes, but neither SubsampledSeeds nor LatticeViewStage predicts it.
5. ObjectnessViewStage reads 'on_object' and 'view_width' of the matched labels, which NearestLabelAssigner returns only with `supervise: object_seeds` and `view_widths: true`. GraspnessFPS and ObjectnessViewStage both predict and supervise the 'objectness' of a seed.
6. ObjectnessViewStage computes its targets from 'dense' matched labels, but CompactLabelAssigner returns 'compact' ones. GraspnessFPS and ObjectnessViewStage both predict and supervise the 'objectness' of a seed.
7. OperationHead as configured reads the seed score 'objectness' when it decodes, but neither SubsampledSeeds nor RomaRotationViewStage predicts it.
8. ScaleBalancedAssigner returns a loss weight per seed, but TemplateViewStage does not apply seed weights, so the weighting would silently do nothing there. OperationHead as configured reads the seed score 'objectness' when it decodes, but neither SubsampledSeeds nor TemplateViewStage predicts it.
9. OperationHead as configured reads the seed score 'objectness' when it decodes, but neither SubsampledSeeds nor TwoVectorViewStage predicts it.

### Assigners

| Component | GSNet | EconomicGrasp | FineGrasp | GraspNet-baseline | Scale-Balanced-Grasp | Class |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `CompactLabelAssigner`<br>preset `compact-label` | ✗ (1) | ✓ own | ✓ own | ✗ (2) | ✗ (2) | **some** |
| `NearestLabelAssigner`<br>preset `nearest-label-object-seeds` | ✓ | ✗ (3) | ✗ (3) | ✓ own | ✓ | **most** |
| `ScaleBalancedAssigner`<br>preset `scale-balanced` | ✗ (4) | ✗ (5) | ✗ (5) | ✓ | ✓ own | **some** |
| `NearestLabelAssigner`<br>constructor defaults | ✓ own | ✗ (3) | ✗ (3) | ✗ (6) | ✗ (6) | **specific** |

1. CompactLabelAssigner returns 'compact' matched labels, but SWADHead is supervised with 'dense' ones. data.train.dataset: transforms[2] (SampleGraspLabels) reads the dense label grids, which a dataset with `compact_labels` does not serve.
2. CompactLabelAssigner returns 'compact' matched labels, but OperationHead is supervised with 'dense' ones. ObjectnessViewStage computes its targets from 'dense' matched labels, but CompactLabelAssigner returns 'compact' ones. data.train.dataset: transforms[2] (SampleGraspLabels) reads the dense label grids, which a dataset with `compact_labels` does not serve.
3. NearestLabelAssigner returns 'dense' matched labels, but EconomicHead is supervised with 'compact' ones.
4. ScaleBalancedAssigner returns a loss weight per seed, but TemplateViewStage and SWADHead do not apply seed weights, so the weighting would silently do nothing there.
5. ScaleBalancedAssigner returns 'dense' matched labels, but EconomicHead is supervised with 'compact' ones. ScaleBalancedAssigner returns a loss weight per seed, but TemplateViewStage and EconomicHead do not apply seed weights, so the weighting would silently do nothing there.
6. ObjectnessViewStage reads 'on_object' and 'view_width' of the matched labels, which NearestLabelAssigner returns only with `supervise: object_seeds` and `view_widths: true`.

1. CompactLabelAssigner returns 'compact' matched labels, but DecoupledGridHead is supervised with 'dense' ones.
2. DepthCylinderGroup emits features with axes ('seed', 'depth', 'channel'), but DecoupledGridHead expects ('seed', 'channel').
3. DepthCylinderGroup emits features with axes ('seed', 'depth', 'channel'), but DecoupledGridHead expects ('seed', 'channel'). ScaleBalancedAssigner returns a loss weight per seed, but DecoupledGridHead does not apply seed weights, so the weighting would silently do nothing there.
4. NearestLabelAssigner returns 'dense' matched labels, but EconomicHead is supervised with 'compact' ones. data.train.dataset: transforms[2] (SampleGraspLabels) reads the dense label grids, which a dataset with `compact_labels` does not serve.
5. DepthCylinderGroup emits features with axes ('seed', 'depth', 'channel'), but EconomicHead expects ('seed', 'channel'). NearestLabelAssigner returns 'dense' matched labels, but EconomicHead is supervised with 'compact' ones. data.train.dataset: transforms[2] (SampleGraspLabels) reads the dense label grids, which a dataset with `compact_labels` does not serve.
6. DepthCylinderGroup emits features with axes ('seed', 'depth', 'channel'), but EconomicHead expects ('seed', 'channel'). ScaleBalancedAssigner returns 'dense' matched labels, but EconomicHead is supervised with 'compact' ones. ScaleBalancedAssigner returns a loss weight per seed, but EconomicHead does not apply seed weights, so the weighting would silently do nothing there. data.train.dataset: transforms[2] (SampleGraspLabels) reads the dense label grids, which a dataset with `compact_labels` does not serve.
7. CylinderGroup emits features with axes ('seed', 'channel'), but OperationHead expects ('seed', 'depth', 'channel').
8. CylinderInteractionGroup emits features with axes ('seed', 'channel'), but OperationHead expects ('seed', 'depth', 'channel'). CompactLabelAssigner returns 'compact' matched labels, but OperationHead is supervised with 'dense' ones.
9. MultiScaleGroup emits features with axes ('seed', 'channel'), but OperationHead expects ('seed', 'depth', 'channel'). CompactLabelAssigner returns 'compact' matched labels, but OperationHead is supervised with 'dense' ones.
10. CompactLabelAssigner returns 'compact' matched labels, but SWADHead is supervised with 'dense' ones.
11. DepthCylinderGroup emits features with axes ('seed', 'depth', 'channel'), but SWADHead expects ('seed', 'channel').
12. DepthCylinderGroup emits features with axes ('seed', 'depth', 'channel'), but SWADHead expects ('seed', 'channel'). ScaleBalancedAssigner returns a loss weight per seed, but SWADHead does not apply seed weights, so the weighting would silently do nothing there.

## The training recipe

A recipe preset changes what is around the model: the optimizer, the schedule, the hooks of the training loop, the point augmentation. Each is applied alone to a method as shipped and probed like a stage. `—`: the preset names the scene encoder of the seed-based skeleton and is probed under a second seed-based method instead of HGGD. What each preset is and how to use it: [the recipe slot](../slots/recipe.md).

What did not run, in the words of the tool:

- `recipe/GSNet/optimizer/schedulefree-sgd` (`runs-unstable`): 1 of 20 iterations had no real seed (iteration 3).
- `recipe/HGGD/optimizer/soap` (`fails`): at step: RuntimeError: CUDA error: an illegal memory access was encountered CUDA kernel errors might be asynchronously reported at some other API call, so the stacktrace below might be incorrect.
- `recipe/GSNet/hooks/amp` (`fails`): at loss, in the assigner NearestLabelAssigner: RuntimeError: Index put requires the source and destination dtypes match, got Float for the destination and Half for the source.
- `recipe/HGGD/hooks/amp` (`fails`): at loss: NonFiniteLossError: non-finite loss at epoch 1, iteration 1: loss/heatmap = nan, loss/angle = inf.
- `recipe/HGGD/augment/jitter` (`fails`): at data, in the transform RandomJitter: ContractError: graspnet1b/scene_0000/realsense/0128: RandomJitter moves points, which would leave the image-space data of this sample behind (rgb, depth, view_grasps).
- `recipe/HGGD/augment/shift` (`fails`): at data, in the transform RandomShift: ContractError: graspnet1b/scene_0000/realsense/0128: RandomShift moves points, which would leave the image-space data of this sample behind (rgb, depth, view_grasps).

## Sets of stages

48 of the 7168 sets were probed: 48 `runs`. A set states all five stages and the encoder: the preset named, under which the set needs no adapter. It was composed onto the method config whose data recipe serves its labels (last but one column), so the optimizer, the schedule and the data pipeline are that method's.

## Post-processing

Every post-processing preset as the evaluation variant `post` of a method (`grasppanda compose <config> --set post=<preset>`), applied by the probe to the predictions of its two frames: grasps predicted → grasps left. A post-processor reads grasps and the observation, never a network, so three methods stand for the three kinds of input: seeds on a dense cloud with the full cloud kept, seeds of a sub-sampling encoder, and HGGD. The grasps are those of a detector trained for the iterations of the probe; [the page of the slot](../slots/post.md) has the same steps on the predictions of released weights.

| preset | GSNet | GraspNet-baseline | HGGD |
|---|---|---|---|

## Losses

Every loss preset in a loss term it is meant for, under GSNet and under one more method (`grasppanda compose <config> --set <stage>.<loss option>=<preset>`). A probe replaces several loss terms of a method at once: the rows between two empty lines are one probed config and share its verdict. The last column is the weighted value of the replaced term at the first and at the last of the 20 iterations: it shows that the term is finite and moves, nothing about accuracy, and values of different losses are not comparable. The last rows are pairings the config check refuses. Which loss fits which term is a contract ([Heads and losses](../slots/head_loss.md)); the unit tests run every loss in every term of its kind on tiny models.

1. SWADHead.width_loss is a `value` term (a prediction and a target of equal shape, the target an unbounded quantity), but FocalLoss fits `class` or `unit` terms.
2. OperationHead.score_loss is a `value` term (a prediction and a target of equal shape, the target an unbounded quantity), but QualityFocal fits `unit` terms.
3. ScaleBalancedAssigner returns a loss weight per seed and OperationHead passes it to angle_loss, but DiceLoss scores the supervised set as a whole and cannot weight single elements.

## Not on this page

- Accuracy of any kind. See the method pages of the [model zoo](../model_zoo.md).
- Other datasets, cameras and recipes than the ones named above.
- Combinations of two or more replaced stages beyond the stage sets.
- Inner parts of HGGD: it has no registered slots yet, so it is probed as it is.
- 7120 cell(s) of the grid that were not probed in this run.

## Adding a component

A new encoder or stage appears in the grid by being registered. Give it a preset if its options cannot be guessed ([Try a combination](../user_guides/combinations.md)), probe its cells and regenerate:

```bash
python -m tools.probe_grid run --only 'encoder/*/MyEncoder' 'stage/*/*/my-preset'
python -m tools.probe_grid export
python -m tools.make_combination_docs
```

`tests/unit/test_combine_grid.py` fails until every cell of a registered component has a record in the measured file.
